q: Will running a second shift lower our CO2 per unit?
title: Second shift and CO2 per unit
short: Often yes, per unit, because fixed loads such as lighting, compressors on standby, furnace holding and offices are spread over more output. Total emissions still rise with production. Report both: absolute tonnes and tonnes per unit, so a buyer does not mistake growth for a worse plant.

ul: Monthly kWh and fuel against units produced.
Base load at zero production, from idle readings.
Per unit figures before and after.

p: If the second shift runs older, less efficient machines, per unit emissions can rise.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
